pages.main_text: Make courageous change Apply Visit us Get Info Apply now for Summer or Fall! We'll walk you through everything you need to know to become a student. Get Started We'd love to meet with you! Come see our campus on a tour or talk with us online in an info session. Connect with us Get helpful updates on programs, deadlines, and other tips about enrolling. What are your goals? Earn a degree, transfer, or launch your career If you’re looking for education and job training that won’t break the bank or a campus that feels more like a community, Lane is the place for you. Get a jump start on your academic and career goals and receive the support you need to launch your future. Learn more about getting started at Lane. Learn more about getting started at Lane Attend Lane as an international student From the moment you land in Eugene to the time you walk across the commencement stage, you’ll receive the support and resources you need to succeed. You’ll also make friends on campus, around Eugene, and in a furnished apartment at our downtown student housing, Titan Court. Learn more about our International Program Earn your GED or prep for college Earn Your GED Complete your GED exam with friendly instructors to support and guide you College Prep Classes Refresh your writing or math skills with our tuition-free college prep classes Learn English as a second language If you’re ready to start or continue learning English, Lane is the right place for you. We offer intensive programs during the day or in the evening to best fit your schedule. Our instructors work with students from all over the world and are there to help you improve your oral and written English skills for whatever your goals may be! Learn more about our ESL options Take classes or explore a hobby for fun You’ll find opportunities to explore your hobbies or nurture new ones in our Continuing Education program. Learn and connect with others in the community with the same interests and develop your love of lifelong learning. Learn more about Continuing Education at Lane Get college credit while in high school College Now Earn both high school and college credit for the same course without leaving your high school at no cost to you! Early College Get an early start on college courses by taking courses at LCC while still enrolled in high school Close Not Sure? Already thinking about a specific career? Explore Programs and Careers 55% less compared to the University of Oregon (tuition & fees, 45 credits) Lane $ U of O $$$ Lane U of O Cut your cost, expand your options Learn more about how to pay for college and ways to make college affordable . We support each other to make anything possible I’ve always wanted to be my own manager and open a business. Any business. Leonardo Kim From an Associate in Automotive to a Bachelor’s in Business We're here for you with support in academics , daily living , careers , and more. Explore Student Support Happening at Lane Sep 10 Drop-in Fall Reg Fest! 1:00pm - 6:00pm Building 1 Admissions 102 Sep 12 Womens Soccer vs Portland 12:00pm - 2:00pm Soccer Field - Turf Sep 12 Mens Soccer vs Chemeketa 2:15pm - 4:15pm Soccer Field - Turf More events Joint Message Regarding NWCCU Special Visit Lane Hosts Second Annual Design Educators Summit, Strengthening Ties Between High School and College Classrooms Lane Community College Celebrates 2026 Commencement More news

pages.main_text: Communication and Support to the Board Policy Number BP 2722 Policy Category Chapter 2 - Board of Education Adopted June 4, 2025 Last Revised March 31, 2026 Last Reviewed March 31, 2026 The President shall assure that the Board of Education is informed and supported in its governance responsibilities. Accordingly, the President shall: Submit reports required by the Board in a timely, accurate, and understandable manner, directly addressing applicable Board policies, goals, and performance expectations. Keep the Board informed of relevant trends, significant issues, anticipated adverse media coverage, or material external and internal changes, particularly changes that may affect Board policies, institutional priorities, or strategic direction. Advise the Board if, in the President's opinion, the Board is not in compliance with its own policies or established governance practices, particularly in cases where Board actions or behavior may be detrimental to effective governance or the working relationship between the Board and the President. Present to the Board sufficient staff and external perspectives, issues, and options to support fully informed Board deliberation and decision-making. Provide a mechanism for official communications from the Board, its officers, or its committees. Communicate with the Board as a whole except when (a) fulfilling individual requests or providing information; or (b) responding to officers or committees duly authorized by the Board. Report in a timely manner any known noncompliance with Board policy or applicable law. Include on the consent agenda items delegated to the President that require Board approval by law or contract, along with the appropriate supporting documentation. Provide semiannual budget planning information to support the Board’s fiscal oversight responsibilities. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: Academic Program Review Policy Number BP 4360 Policy Category Chapter 4 - Academic Affairs Adopted June 4, 2025 Last Reviewed January 7, 2026 In order to ensure that the academic programs and services offered by the college continue to be of the highest possible quality, the President shall ensure that all academic programs and services will engage in a formal process of review designed to assess and enhance program effectiveness. The review process will be outcomes-based, data-driven, and implemented by the program itself. It will involve identification of quality indicators appropriate to the program, measurable baselines, and measurable progress toward improvement as needed. Reviews will occur on an ongoing, cyclical basis. The program review will evaluate: whether educational or service objectives are consistent with the college's mission or purpose the achievement of students in relation to the intended educational outcomes identified the extent to which the college regularly uses the results of program or service review for improvement of its programs and services. References Note: This policy replaced retired Board Policy 035. The language from the former three-digit policy was adopted without change for this new four-digit policy number. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: Accreditation Policy Number BP 3200 Policy Category Chapter 3 - General Institution Adopted December 15, 2021 Last Reviewed June 3, 2026 The President shall ensure Lane Community College complies with the accreditation process and standards of the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities (NWCCU) (accreditation standards of the Northwest Commission on Colleges and Universities) and of other Lane Community College programs that seek special accreditation. The President shall keep the Board of Education informed of approved accrediting organizations and the status of accreditations. The President shall ensure that the Board of Education is involved in any accreditation process in which Board of Education participation is required. The President shall provide the Board of Education with a summary of any accreditation report and any actions taken or to be taken in response to recommendations in an accreditation report. pages.main_text: Admissions and Concurrent Enrollment Policy Number BP 5010 Policy Category Chapter 5 - Student Services Adopted February 1, 2023 Last Reviewed February 1, 2023 Lane Community College accepts all students who are 18 or over or have a high school diploma or GED. Students who are under 18 and have not graduated may still attend if they follow the guidelines for Under 18 Students. Under no circumstances shall an applicant who is otherwise qualified be denied admission or given a preference for admission to the college based on an individual's race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender stereotypes, parental status, national origin, perceived shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics, age, limited English proficiency or English learner status, physical or mental disability, record of or regarded as having a disability, genetic information, family relationship, marital status, expunged juvenile record, veteran status or political affiliation or association with any member of these protected groups. Lane Community College shall in its discretion, or as otherwise federally mandated, evaluate the validity of a student’s high school completion.  The President shall establish procedures for evaluating the validity of a student’s high school completion. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: Advertising Policy Number BP 3450 Policy Category Chapter 3 - General Institution Adopted June 4, 2025 Last Revised March 4, 2026 Last Reviewed March 24, 2026 Advertisements shall relate to the mission, vision, and core values of the College. Advertisements shall tell the truth and shall reveal significant facts, the omission of which would mislead the public. Advertisers are responsible for providing accurate copy. Prior to making advertising claims, advertisers shall have in their possession documents that substantiate such claims. Lane Community College reserves the right to refuse any advertisement at any time, including, but not limited to, the following: Advertisements that are deemed to wrongfully discriminate on the basis of age, sex, race, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, disability, familial relationship, marital status, gender identity, pregnancy, veteran status, or expunged record. Advertisements deemed to contain statements, illustrations or implications which are not consistent with the College's mission and vision. Advertisements for any product or service which if purchased by a qualified individual would be in violation of any law. Advertisements bearing the name/logo "Lane Community College" or "LCC" must be approved by the College. This policy applies to all forms of advertising and promotional materials, regardless of medium, including print, digital, broadcast, and emerging communication platforms. The College President shall be responsible for implementing this policy and may delegate authority as necessary to carry out its provisions. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: Student Success and Support Services Policy Number BP 5005 Policy Category Chapter 5 - Student Services Adopted June 4, 2025 Last Revised January 7, 2026 Last Reviewed January 7, 2026 Student success is at the heart of Lane's mission, and the foundation upon which faculty and staff shall organize and plan their work to achieve Lane's vision of transforming lives through learning. Lane Community College supports student success by providing opportunity and access to student services for all eligible students. The College will: Ensure there is equity in access, participation, and success across all educational programs and college services. Maintain an environment that is welcoming and accepting to all students. Provide appropriate resources and protocols to promote the physical and emotional safety of students throughout the learning environment. Ensure all official communications, including catalogs, official statements, promotional materials, and digital platforms, accurately represent the institution and its programs. Collect only information necessary for educational and administrative purposes and ensure that student data is collected, stored, reviewed, and transmitted securely in compliance with state and federal regulations. Design student service spaces and practices to uphold confidentiality and provide a reasonable level of privacy for conversations and interactions. Clearly inform students of available services, including the scope, limitations, and expected outcomes of those services. Provide students with accessible information regarding their rights and responsibilities, along with clear, fair processes to address concerns, complaints, or grievances. The President is responsible for implementing this policy through administrative procedures and practices that uphold these principles and support continuous improvement in student services. . References Note: This policy replaces retired Board Policy 720 (last reviewed April 4, 2023). The language has been adopted without change and renumbered to align with the four-digit policy structure. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: Education Records, Directory Information, and Privacy Policy Number BP 5040 Policy Category Chapter 5 - Student Services Adopted March 17, 2021 Last Revised January 7, 2026 Last Reviewed January 7, 2026 The President shall assure that student records are maintained in compliance with applicable federal and state laws relating to the privacy of student records. The President may direct the implementation of appropriate safeguards to assure that student records cannot be accessed or modified by any person not authorized to do so. Any currently enrolled or former student of Lane Community College has a right of access to any and all student records relating to them maintained by Lane Community College. No representative of Lane Community College shall release the contents of a student record to any member of the public without the prior written consent of the student, other than directory information as defined in this policy and information sought pursuant to a court order or lawfully issued subpoena, or as otherwise authorized by applicable federal and state laws. Students shall be notified of their rights with respect to student records, including the definition of directory information contained here, and that they may limit the information. Directory information may include the student’s: Name and address, telephone listing, electronic mail address; Photograph; Date and place of birth; Major field of study; Grade level; Enrollment status (e.g., undergraduate or graduate, full-time or part-time); Dates of attendance; Participation in officially recognized activities and sports; Weight and height, if a member of an athletic team; Degrees, honors, and awards received; and Most recent educational agency or institution attended Directory information does not include a student’s: Social security number; and Student identification number Federal Immigration Authority Access to Student Records Oregon law prohibits disclosure of student records to federal immigration authorities for the purpose of enforcing federal immigration laws. Federal and state laws also make student records confidential and permit their disclosure only in limited circumstances. To assure compliance with applicable federal and state law, Lane Community College’s employees shall not disclose student records, or information from those records, to federal immigration authorities except as allowed by this policy and College procedures. Board Policies are adopted by the Lane Community College Board of Education and establish the College’s governing principles and institutional direction. These policies are reviewed by the Board at least every five years or more often as needed. Board Policies are distinct from College Operating Policies and Procedures (COPPS), which provide operational guidance and are developed through governance processes and by responsible managers.

pages.main_text: LCC board meets March 18 by remote method March 16, 2020 schmidtk EUGENE, Ore.– The Lane Community College Board of Education will meet Wednesday, March 18, at 6 p.m., via teleconference, as a precaution due to the COVID-19 situation. Public accessibility will be made available via Zoom video conferencing or similar remote delivery; instructions are available to access the meeting . Discussion/action items on the agenda: Emergency Management - Discussion Pacific University Agreement - Action Building 19 Pacific University Renovation - Action Bond Update - Discussion Budget Projection - Discussion Tuition and Fees - Action For more information contact Donna Zmolek, Executive Assistant to the President and Board, at zmolekd@lanecc.edu or (541) 463-5301. For more information about Lane Community College: www.lanecc.edu/Newsroom twitter.com/LaneTitans www.facebook.com/LaneCommunityCollege Lane is an AA/EEO/Veterans/Disabilities Employer ### Media Contact Donna Zmolek, Executive Assistant to the President and Board Phone (541) 463-5301 Lane Community College educates over 25,000 students annually at six locations across Lane County and online. Students and alumni from all 50 states and 79 countries create more than an $850 million dollar impact on the local economy, helping to support more than 13,000 local jobs. Lane provides affordable, quality, professional technical and college transfer programs; business development and employee training; academic, language and life skills development; and lifelong personal development and enrichment courses.
